title: Linear Search
description: Understand how linear search works and learn why sequential scanning is one of the simplest searching techniques.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Searching is one of the most common operations in computer science.

Applications constantly search through data collections such as usernames, products, files, or records.

Linear search is one of the simplest searching algorithms because it examines elements one-by-one until the target value is found.

sections.title: How Linear Search Works
sections.content:
Linear search scans data sequentially from the beginning of the collection toward the end.

The algorithm compares each element with the target value.

If a match is found, the search stops immediately. Otherwise, the algorithm continues until all elements have been checked.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Search Process
sections.content:
Suppose an array contains several numbers and the algorithm must locate a specific value.

The search begins at the first element. If the value does not match, the algorithm moves to the next element.

This process repeats continuously until the target is discovered or the entire array has been scanned.

Because every element may need to be checked, linear search has linear time complexity.

sections.title: Advantages and Limitations
sections.content:
Linear search is extremely simple to understand and implement.

It works even when the data is unsorted, making it flexible for many beginner-level problems.

However, linear search becomes inefficient for very large datasets because the algorithm may need to inspect every element individually.

sections.title: Searching Through a Backpack
sections.content:
Imagine searching for a specific notebook inside a backpack.

Without any organized arrangement, the easiest strategy is to inspect items one-by-one until the notebook is found.

This mirrors how linear search works when scanning through data sequentially.

sections.title: Linear Search in Real Applications
sections.content:
Linear search is commonly used for small datasets or situations where the data is not sorted.

Many beginner systems and simple applications rely on sequential scanning because it is straightforward and reliable.

Although more advanced search algorithms exist, linear search remains important because it introduces the fundamental idea of searching through data collections.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: Linear search scans elements sequentially until the target value is found. It is simple, flexible, and works on unsorted data, but its performance becomes slower as dataset size increases.
